newsitem.title: GERMANY: Further stoppages possible at Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: Further stoppages possible at Lufthansa.

text.p: The German trade union involved in a pay dispute with German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Wednesday it would not rule out further limited stoppages.

German white-collar union DAG, which represents sections of Lufthansa's air and ground staff, has already this month organised a stoppage which grounded 35 Lufthansa flights and cost the airline millions of marks in lost business.
"Further industrial action by the DAG cannot be ruled out at Lufthansa," it said in a statement.
DAG added that Lufthansa had not budged on its wage offer or the length of the contracts it is asking employees to sign.
DAG believes that the 27-month contracts Lufthansa is offering would give the airline room to introduce new labour cost-cutting measures unopposed.
The union said Lufthansa was offering some 50,000 employees a one-time payment of one-third of a month's salary plus a 1.7 percent wage increase up to the end of 1998.
It has said it want a rise of four percent a year.
